If riches increase, set not thine heart upon them. Ps. 62:10.

Introduction

He was 87 years old, and felt himself (as he himself wrote) as one “with dim eyes, shaking hands, and tottering feet.” But he had a message to give yet. With a vehemence that seems even greater than his normal fervency, John Wesley warned of a great danger to his people—riches. From a small handful, his movement had grown to 135,000 members with over 500 itinerant preachers. His preaching was effective in noticeably changing the moral and ethical climate of England, to the point that he is credited with saving England from a bloodbath like later happened in the French Revolution. But a sinister evil lurked among his people, and Wesley used some of his last remaining strength to call this evil for what it was.

May we who are many times richer than the people of John Wesley’s day have ears to hear.

(Note that some of Wesley’s English has been updated and that the subtitles are not original. The signature under the title is a facsimile of his own signature.)

From that express declaration of our Lord, “It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven,” we may easily learn that none can have riches without being greatly endangered by them. But if the danger of barely having them is so great, how much greater is the danger of increasing them! This danger is great even to those who receive what is transmitted to them by their forefathers; but it is abundantly greater to those who acquire them by their skill and industry. Therefore, nothing can be more prudent than this caution: “If riches increase, set not thine heart upon them.” Ps. 62:10

It is true, riches, and the increase of them, are the gift of God. Yet great care is to be taken that what is intended for a blessing does not turn into a curse. To prevent this, it is highly expedient to consider seriously:

  1. What is meant by riches; and when they may be said to increase.
  2. What is implied in setting our hearts upon them; and how we may avoid it.

What does “riches” mean?

Consider, first, what is here meant by riches. Indeed some may imagine that it is hardly possible to mistake the meaning of this common word. Yet, in truth, there are thousands in this mistake; and many of them quite innocently. A person of note, hearing a sermon preached upon this subject several years ago, between surprise and indignation broke out aloud, “Why does he talk about riches here? There is no rich man at Whitehaven, except Sir James L----r.”

And it is true there was none but he that had £40,0001 a year, and some millions in ready money. But a man may be rich that has not £100 a year, nor even £1000 in cash. Whosoever has food to eat, and raiment to put on, with something over, is rich. Whoever has the necessaries and conveniences of life for himself and his family, and a little to spare for them that have not, is properly a rich man; unless he is a miser, a lover of money, one that hoards up what he can and ought to give to the poor. For if so, he is a poor man still, though he has millions in the bank; yea, he is the poorest of men; for:

The beggars but a common lot deplore;
The rich poor man’s emphatically poor.

Beware of judging

But here an exception may be made. A person may have more than necessaries and conveniences for his family, and yet not be rich. For he may be in debt; and his debts may amount to more than he is worth. But if this be the case, he is not a rich man, how much money soever he has in his hands. Yea, a man of business may be afraid that this is the real condition of his affairs, whether it be or no; and then he cannot be so charitable as he would, for fear of being unjust. How many that are engaged in trade are in this very condition! Those especially that trade to a very large amount; for their affairs are frequently so entangled that it is not possible to determine, with any exactness, how much they are worth, or, indeed, whether they are worth anything or nothing. Should we not make a fair allowance for them?

And beware of forming a hasty judgment concerning the fortune of others. There may be secrets in the situation of a person, which few but God are acquainted with. Some years ago, I told a gentleman, “Sir, I am afraid you are covetous.”

He asked me, “What is the reason of your fear?”

I answered, “A year ago, when I made a collection for the expense of repairing the Foundery, you subscribed five guineas. At the subscription made this year you subscribed only half a guinea.”

He made no reply; but after a time asked, “Pray, sir, answer me a question: Why do you live upon potatoes?” (I did so between three and four years.)

I replied, “It has much conduced to my health.”

He answered, “I believe it has. But did you not do it likewise to save money?”

I said, “I did; for what I save from my own food expense will feed another that else would have none.”

“But, sir,” said he, “if this be your motive you may save much more. I know a man that goes to the market at the beginning of every week: There he buys a pennyworth of parsnips, which he boils in a large quantity of water. The parsnips serve him for food, and the water for drink the whole following week. So his meat and drink together cost him only a penny a week.”

This he constantly did, though he earned then £200/year,2 so that he could pay the debts which he had contracted before he knew God! And this was he, whom I had set down for a covetous man!

What about you?

But there are those who are conscious before God that they are rich. And, doubtless, some among you are of the number. You have more of the goods of this world than is needful either for yourself or your family. Let each consider for himself. Do your riches increase? Do not you understand that plain expression? Have you not more money, or more of money’s worth, than you had 10 or 20 years ago, or at this time last year? If you keep any account, you can easily know this. Indeed you ought to know; otherwise, you are not a good steward, even in this respect, of the mammon of unrighteousness. And every man, whether engaged in trade or not, ought to know whether his substance lessens or increases.

But many have found out a way never to be rich, though their substance increase ever so much. It is this: As fast as money comes in they invest it, either in land or enlarging their business. By this means each of these, by keeping his cash assets low, can still say, “I am not rich.” He can say that even though he has 10, 20, or 100 times more substance than he had some years ago.

This may be explained by a recent case: A gentleman came to a merchant in London a few years ago and told him, “Sir, I beg you will give me a guinea3 for a worthy family that is in great distress.”

He replied, “Really, Mr. M., I cannot well afford to give you it just now; but if you will call upon me when I am worth £10,000, then I will give you ten guineas.”

Mr. M., after some time, called upon him again and said, “Sir, I claim your promise; now you are worth £10,000.”

He replied, “That is very true: But I assure you, I cannot spare one guinea so well as I could then.”

It is possible for a man to cheat himself by this ingenious device. And he may cheat other men; for as long “as you doest good unto yourself, men will speak well of thee.” “A right good man,” says the Londoner, “he is worth a plum” (£100,000). But, alas! he cannot deceive God; and he cannot deceive the devil. Ah, no! The curse of God is upon thee already, and on all that you have. And tomorrow, when the devil seizes your soul, will he not say, “What do all your riches profit you?” Will they purchase a pillow for your head, in the lake of fire burning with brimstone? Or will they procure you a cup of “water to cool your tongue,” while you are tormented in that flame?” O follow the wise direction here given so that God may not say unto thee, “Thou fool!”

This mental gymnastics, therefore, will not avail. It will not be any protection either against the wrath of God or the malice and power of the devil. You are convicted already of “setting thy heart” upon your riches, if you reinvest all you have above the conveniences of life, on adding money to money, house to house, or field to field, without giving at least a tenth of your income (the Jewish proportion) to the poor. By whatsoever means your riches increase, whether with or without labour; whether by trade, inheritances, or any other way; unless your charities increase in the same proportion; unless you give a full tenth of your substance, of your fixed and occasional income; you undoubtedly set your heart upon your gold, and it will “eat thy flesh as fire!”4

The hardheartedness of the covetousness

But O! who can convince a rich man that he sets his heart upon riches? For considerably above half a century I have spoken on this head, with all the plainness that was in my power. But with how little effect! I doubt whether I have, in all that time, convinced fifty misers of covetousness. When the lover of money was described ever so clearly, and painted in the strongest colors, who applied it to himself? To whom did God, and all that knew him, say, “Thou art the man!” If He speaks to any of you that are present, O do not stop your ears! Rather say, with Zaccheus, “Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have done any wrong to any man, I restore fourfold.” He did not mean that he had done this in time past; but that he determined to do so for the time to come. I charge thee before God, you lover of money, to “go and do likewise!”

I have a message from God unto thee, O rich man! whether you wilt hear, or whether you wilt forbear. Riches have increased with thee; at the peril of your soul, “set not thine heart upon them!” Be thankful to Him that gave thee such a talent, so much power of doing good. Yet dare not to rejoice over them, but with fear and trembling, “Beware you cleave not unto them, lest you be entangled and perish.” Do not make them your end, your chief delight, your happiness, your god! See that you expect not happiness in money, nor anything that is purchasable thereby; in gratifying either the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, or the pride of life.

But let us descend to particulars; and see that each of you deal faithfully with his own soul. If any of you have now twice, thrice, or four times as much substance as when you first saw my face, faithfully examine yourselves and see if you do not set your hearts, if not directly on money or riches themselves, yet on some of the things that are purchasable thereby; which comes to the same thing. All those the Apostle John includes under that general name, the world; and the desire of them, or to seek happiness in them, under that form, “the love of the world.”

Defining “the world”

This he divides into three branches, “the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life.” Fairly examine yourselves with regard to these.

  • First, as to “the desire of the flesh.” I believe this means the seeking of happiness in the things that gratify the senses. To instance in one: Do not you seek your happiness in enlarging the pleasure of tasting? To be more particular: Do you not eat more plentifully, or more delicately, than you did ten or twenty years ago? Do not you use more drink, or drink of a more costly kind, than you did then? Do you sleep on as hard a bed as you did once, supposing your health will bear it? To touch on one point more: do you fast as often, now that you are rich, as you did when you were poor? Ought you not, in all reason, to do this rather more often than more seldom? I am afraid your own heart condemns you. You are not clear in this matter.
  • The second branch of the love of the world, “the desire of the eyes,” is of a wider extent. We may understand thereby the seeking our happiness in gratifying the imagination, (which is chiefly done by means of the eyes,) by grand, or new, or beautiful objects (if they may not all be reduced to one head; since neither grand nor beautiful objects are pleasing when the novelty of them is gone). But are not the hollowest things pleasing as long as they are new? Do not some of you, on the score of novelty, seek no small part of your happiness in that hollowest of hollows—dress? Do you not bestow more money, or (which is the same) more time or pains upon it than you did once? I doubt this is not done to please God. Then it pleases the devil. If you laid aside your needless ornaments some years ago—ruffles, necklaces, spider-caps, ugly and unbecoming bonnets,5 costly linen, expensive laces—have you not, in defiance of religion and reason, taken to them again?6

Perhaps you say you can now afford the expense. This is the quintessence of nonsense. Who gave you this addition to your fortune; or (to speak properly) lent it to you? To speak more properly still, who lodged it for a time in your hands as His stewards; informing you at the same time for what purposes He entrusted you with it? And can you afford to waste your Lord’s goods, for every part of which you are to give an account; or to expend them in any other way than that which He hath expressly appointed? Away with this vile, diabolical chant! Let it never more come out of your lips. This affording to rob God is the very chant of hell.

Do not you know that God entrusted you with that money (all that is above what buys necessaries for your families) to feed the hungry, to clothe the naked, to help the stranger, the widow, the fatherless; and, indeed, as far as it will go, to relieve the wants of all mankind? How can you, how dare you, defraud your Lord by applying it to any other purpose? When He entrusted you with a little, did He not entrust you with it that you might lay out all that little in doing good? And when He entrusted you with more, did He not entrust you with that additional money that you might do so much the more good, as you had more ability? Had you any more right to waste a pound, a shilling, or a penny, than you had before? You have, therefore, no more right to gratify the desire of the flesh, or the desire of the eyes, now than when you were a beggar. O no! do not make so poor a return to your beneficent Lord! Rather, the more He entrusts you with, be so much the more careful to employ every mite as He hath appointed.

Employing mites as do the angels

Ye angels of God, ye servants of His that continually do His pleasure: our common Lord hath entrusted you also with talents far more precious than gold and silver so that you may minister in your various offices to the heirs of salvation. Do not you employ every mite of what you have received to the end for which it was given you? And hath He not directed us to do His will on earth, as it is done by you in heaven? Brethren, what are we doing! Let us awake! Let us arise! Let us imitate those flaming ministers! Let us employ our whole soul, body, and substance according to the will of our Lord! Let us render unto God the things that are God’s; even all we are, and all we have!

Most of those who set their hearts upon riches increase when they increase, do it indirectly, as in some of the preceding instances I related. But there are others who do this more directly, being, properly, “lovers of money.” These love it for its own sake; not only for the sake of what it procures. But this vice is very rarely found in children or young persons; but only, or chiefly, in the old—in those that have the least need of money, and the least time to enjoy it.

Might not this induce one to think that in many cases it is a penal evil; that it is a sin-punishing evil; that when a man has, for many years, hid his precious talent in the earth, God delivers him up to Satan, to punish by the inordinate love of it? Then it is that he is more and more tormented by that “that execrable hunger after gold” which can never be satisfied. No, it is most true, as the very heathen observes: “As money, so the love of money grows; it increases in the same proportion.” As in a dropsy; the more you drink, the more you thirst, till that unquenchable thirst plunges you into the fire which shall never be quenched!

“But is there no way,” you may ask, “either to prevent or to cure this dire disease?” There is one preventative of it, which is also a remedy for it; and I believe there is no other under heaven. It is this. After you have gained (with the cautions above given) all you can, and saved all you can, wanting for nothing; spend not one pound, one shilling, or one penny to gratify either the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, or the pride of life; or indeed, for any other end than to please and glorify God. Having avoided this rock on the right hand, beware of that on the left. Secondly. Hoard nothing. Lay up no treasure on earth, but give all you can; that is, all you have. I defy all the men upon earth, yea, all the angels in heaven, to find any other way of extracting the poison from riches.

Wesley’s last advice

Let me add one word more. After having served you between sixty and seventy years; with dim eyes, shaking hands, and tottering feet, I give you one more advice before I sink into the dust. Mark those words of St. Paul: “Those that desire” or endeavour “to be rich,” that moment “fall into temptation.” Yea, a deep gulf of temptation, out of which nothing less than almighty power can deliver them. “They fall into a snare”—the word properly means a steel trap, which instantly crushes the animal taken therein to pieces—“and into divers foolish and hurtful desires, which plunge men into destruction and perdition.” You, above all men, who now prosper in the world, never forget these awful words! How unspeakably slippery is your path! How dangerous every step! The Lord God enable you to see your danger, and make you deeply sensible of it! O may you “awake up after His likeness, and be satisfied with it!”

Permit me to come a little closer still. Perhaps I may not trouble you any more on this subject. I am pained for you that are “rich in this world.” Do you give all you can? You who receive £500 a year, and spend only £200, do you give £300 back to God? If not, you certainly rob God of that £300. You that receive £200, and spend but £100, do you give God the £100? If not, you rob Him of just so much.

Excuses

“Nay, may I not do what I will with my own?” Here lies the ground of your mistake. It is not your own. It cannot be, unless you are Lord of heaven and earth.

“However, I must provide for my children.” Certainly. But how? By making them rich? Then you will probably make them heathens, as some of you have done already.

“What shall I do, then?” Lord, speak to their hearts, or else the preacher speaks in vain! Leave them enough to live on, not in idleness and luxury, but by honest industry. And if you have not children, upon what scriptural or rational principle can you leave a groat behind you more than will bury you? I pray consider, what are you the better for what you leave behind you? What does it signify, whether you leave behind you £10,000, or 10,000 shoes and boots?

O leave nothing behind you! Send all you have before you into a better world! Lend it, lend it all unto the Lord, and it shall be paid you again! Is there any danger that His truth should fail? It is fixed as the pillars of heaven. Haste, haste, my brethren, haste—lest you be called away before you settled what you have on this security! When this is done, you may boldly say, “Now I have nothing to do but to die! Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit! Come, Lord Jesus! Come quickly!” ~

1 £ is the symbol for the British pound. Money values are somewhat difficult to determine across the centuries and cultures. But to give a general idea, a common laborer in England in 1780 may have earned £2-3/month. This would be comparable to making approx. $300-400/month in the US economy today.

2 As mentioned in the previous footnote, the average wage for a common laborer of that time was probably in the £30/year range.

3 Approxiamately £1.

4 Wesley’s mention of a tithe here can seem to be that he is only encouraging to give a regular tithe. But notice that the context is of “reinvestment.” Many feel that they should reinvest profits so that they can then earn more, and hence have more to give later. Wesley doubts such “wisdom” and encourages a minimum of 10% to be given to the poor immediately rather than reinvested. The idea of reinvesting profits so as to have more to give later is loaded with temptation. Many seem to never get past reinvesting, and instead of giving more later they just reinvest again ... and again ... and again. And the money never does make it to the poor.

5 Without a doubt Wesley is speaking of a certain stylish bonnet that he felt was ugly, not bonnets in general.

6 Wesley never does get around, in this message, to expounding the third aspect, “the pride of life.”

Mali zikiongezeka, usiweke moyo wako juu yake. Zab. 62:10.

Utangulizi

Alikuwa na umri wa miaka 87, na alijihisi (kama alivyoandika mwenyewe) kuwa mtu “mwenye macho hafifu, mikono inayotetemeka, na miguu inayoyumba.” Lakini bado alikuwa na ujumbe wa kutoa. Kwa msisitizo unaoonekana kuwa mkubwa hata kuliko bidii yake ya kawaida, John Wesley alionya watu wake kuhusu hatari kubwa—utajiri. Kutoka katika kundi dogo, vuguvugu lake lilikuwa limekua na kufikia wanachama 135,000 pamoja na wahubiri wasafiri zaidi ya 500. Mahubiri yake yalikuwa na matokeo katika kubadili kwa kiasi kikubwa hali ya maadili na mwenendo wa Uingereza, kiasi kwamba anasifiwa kwa kuiokoa Uingereza dhidi ya umwagaji damu kama ule uliotokea baadaye katika Mapinduzi ya Ufaransa. Lakini uovu wa kutisha ulikuwa umejificha miongoni mwa watu wake, na Wesley alitumia sehemu ya nguvu zake za mwisho kuuita uovu huo kwa jina lake.

Sisi tulio matajiri mara nyingi zaidi kuliko watu wa siku za John Wesley na tuwe na masikio ya kusikia.

(Kumbuka kwamba baadhi ya Kiingereza cha Wesley kimefanyiwa masasisho na kwamba vichwa vidogo si vya asili. Saini iliyo chini ya kichwa ni nakala inayofanana na saini yake mwenyewe.)

Kutokana na tamko hilo la wazi la Bwana wetu, “Ni rahisi ngamia kupenya tundu la sindano kuliko tajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa mbinguni,” tunaweza kujifunza kwa urahisi kwamba hakuna mtu anayeweza kuwa na mali bila kuwa katika hatari kubwa kwa sababu yake. Lakini ikiwa hatari ya kuwa nazo tu ni kubwa hivyo, hatari ya kuongeza mali hizo ni kubwa zaidi kadiri gani! Hatari hii ni kubwa hata kwa wale wanaopokea urithi kutoka kwa mababu zao; lakini ni kubwa zaidi kwa wale wanaozipata kwa ustadi na bidii yao. Kwa hiyo, hakuna jambo lenye busara zaidi kuliko tahadhari hii: “Mali zikiongezeka, usiweke moyo wako juu yake.” Zab. 62:10

Ni kweli, mali na ongezeko lake ni zawadi ya Mungu. Hata hivyo, tunapaswa kuwa waangalifu sana ili kile kilichokusudiwa kuwa baraka kisigeuke kuwa laana. Ili kuzuia jambo hili, ni muhimu sana kutafakari kwa uzito:

  1. Mali humaanisha nini; na ni wakati gani inaweza kusemwa kwamba zinaongezeka.
  2. Ni nini kinachomaanishwa na kuweka mioyo yetu juu yake; na tunawezaje kuepuka kufanya hivyo.

“Mali” humaanisha nini?

Kwanza, fikiria maana ya mali hapa. Kwa kweli, huenda wengine wakadhani kwamba haiwezekani kabisa kukosea maana ya neno hili la kawaida. Hata hivyo, kwa hakika, maelfu ya watu wamekosea kuhusu maana hii; na wengi wao wamekosea bila kukusudia. Mtu mashuhuri, baada ya kusikiliza mahubiri kuhusu mada hii miaka kadhaa iliyopita, alisema kwa sauti, akiwa amechanganyikiwa na kukasirika: “Kwa nini anazungumza kuhusu utajiri hapa? Hakuna tajiri Whitehaven isipokuwa Sir James L----r.”

Na ni kweli kwamba hakuna mwingine ila yeye aliyekuwa na £40,0001 kwa mwaka, pamoja na mamilioni ya pesa taslimu. Lakini mtu anaweza kuwa tajiri hata kama hana £100 kwa mwaka, wala hata £1000 taslimu. Yeyote aliye na chakula cha kula na mavazi ya kuvaa, pamoja na kitu cha ziada, ni tajiri. Yeyote aliye na mahitaji na mahitaji ya ziada ya maisha kwa ajili yake mwenyewe na familia yake, na kiasi kidogo cha kuwapa wale wasio navyo, kwa hakika ni tajiri; isipokuwa awe bahili, mpenda pesa, anayehodhi kile anachoweza na anachopaswa kuwapa maskini. Kwa maana ikiwa ndivyo, bado ni maskini, ingawa ana mamilioni benki; naam, ndiye maskini kuliko watu wote; kwa maana:

Maskini hulalamikia tu hali ya kawaida ya wote;
Maskini tajiri ni maskini kabisa.

Jihadhari na kutoa hukumu

Hata hivyo, hapa kunaweza kuwekwa kigezo cha pekee. Mtu anaweza kuwa na zaidi ya mahitaji ya lazima na ya ziada kwa ajili ya familia yake, lakini asiwe tajiri. Kwa maana anaweza kuwa na madeni; na madeni yake yanaweza kuzidi thamani ya mali zake. Lakini ikiwa ndivyo ilivyo, yeye si tajiri, hata awe na pesa kiasi gani mikononi mwake. Naam, mfanyabiashara anaweza kuogopa kwamba hali halisi ya mambo yake iko hivyo, iwe ni kweli au la; na hapo hawezi kuwa mkarimu kadiri anavyotaka, kwa kuogopa kutokuwa mwadilifu. Ni watu wangapi wanaojihusisha na biashara walio katika hali hii hii! Hasa wale wanaofanya biashara kwa kiwango kikubwa sana; kwa maana mambo yao mara nyingi yamechanganyika kiasi kwamba haiwezekani kubaini kwa usahihi kiasi cha mali zao, au hata kama wana mali yoyote au hawana. Je, hatupaswi kuwavumilia kwa haki?

Na jihadhari kutoa hukumu ya haraka kuhusu mali za wengine. Huenda kukawa na mambo ya siri katika hali ya mtu ambayo ni wachache tu, isipokuwa Mungu, wanaoyafahamu. Miaka kadhaa iliyopita, nilimwambia bwana mmoja, “Bwana, ninaogopa kwamba wewe ni mchoyo.”

Akaniuliza, “Una sababu gani ya kuogopa hivyo?”

Nikamjibu, “Mwaka mmoja uliopita, nilipokusanya michango kwa ajili ya gharama za kukarabati Foundery, ulitoa guineas tano. Katika mchango wa mwaka huu ulitoa guinea nusu tu.”

Hakujibu; lakini baada ya muda akaniuliza, “Tafadhali, bwana, nijibu swali: Kwa nini unaishi kwa kula viazi?” (Nilifanya hivyo kwa miaka kati ya mitatu na minne.)

Nikamjibu, “Jambo hilo limechangia sana afya yangu.”

Akajibu, “Ninaamini limechangia. Lakini je, hukufanya hivyo pia ili kuokoa pesa?”

Nikasema, “Ndiyo; kwa maana kile ninachookoa kwenye gharama za chakula changu humlisha mtu mwingine ambaye la sivyo hangekuwa na chakula.”

“Lakini, bwana,” akasema, “ikiwa hiyo ndiyo sababu yako, unaweza kuokoa pesa nyingi zaidi. Namjua mtu anayeenda sokoni mwanzoni mwa kila juma: Huko hununua kiasi cha parsnip cha senti moja, ambacho huchemsha kwenye maji mengi. Parsnip humlisha, na maji hunywa kwa juma zima linalofuata. Hivyo basi, chakula na kinywaji chake kwa pamoja humgharimu senti moja tu kwa juma.”

Alifanya hivyo daima, ingawa wakati huo alipata £200 kwa mwaka,2 ili aweze kulipa madeni aliyokuwa amejitwisha kabla hajamjua Mungu! Na huyo ndiye niliyemhukumu kuwa mtu mchoyo!

Na wewe je?

Lakini kuna watu wanaojua mbele za Mungu kwamba wao ni matajiri. Bila shaka, baadhi ya ninyi ni miongoni mwao. Mna mali nyingi zaidi za ulimwengu huu kuliko zinazohitajika kwa ajili yenu wenyewe au familia zenu. Kila mmoja na ajitathmini. Je, mali zenu zinaongezeka? Je, hamuelewi usemi huo ulio wazi? Je, hamna pesa nyingi zaidi, au thamani kubwa zaidi ya pesa, kuliko mliyokuwa nayo miaka 10 au 20 iliyopita, au wakati huu mwaka jana? Ikiwa mnaweka kumbukumbu yoyote, mnaweza kujua jambo hili kwa urahisi. Kwa kweli, mnapaswa kujua; la sivyo, hata katika jambo hili hammo wasimamizi wazuri wa mali ya udhalimu. Na kila mtu, awe anafanya biashara au la, anapaswa kujua kama mali zake zinapungua au zinaongezeka.

Lakini wengi wamegundua njia ya kutokuwa matajiri kamwe, hata mali zao zikiongezeka kiasi gani. Njia hiyo ni hii: Mara tu pesa zinapoingia, wanaziwekeza, ama katika ardhi au kupanua biashara zao. Kwa njia hii, kila mmoja wao, kwa kudumisha kiasi kidogo cha pesa taslimu alicho nacho, bado anaweza kusema, “Mimi si tajiri.” Anaweza kusema hivyo hata kama ana mali mara 10, 20, au 100 zaidi ya alizokuwa nazo miaka kadhaa iliyopita.

Jambo hili linaweza kufafanuliwa kwa kisa cha hivi karibuni: Miaka kadhaa iliyopita, bwana mmoja alimwendea mfanyabiashara jijini London na kumwambia, “Bwana, nakuomba unipe guinea3 kwa ajili ya familia inayostahili kusaidiwa na iliyo katika dhiki kubwa.”

Akajibu, “Kwa kweli, Bw. M., siwezi kumudu kukupa sasa hivi; lakini ukinijia nitakapokuwa na mali ya £10,000, nitakupa guineas kumi.”

Baada ya muda, Bw. M. alimwendea tena na kusema, “Bwana, nakudai utimize ahadi yako; sasa una mali ya £10,000.”

Akajibu, “Hilo ni kweli kabisa: Lakini ninakuhakikishia, sasa siwezi kujinyima hata guinea moja kwa urahisi kama nilivyoweza wakati ule.”

Inawezekana mtu akajidanganya kwa mbinu hii ya ujanja. Na anaweza kuwadanganya watu wengine; kwa maana “maadamu unajifanyia mema, watu watakusifu.” “Ni mtu mwema kabisa,” asema mkazi wa London, “ana mali ya plum” (£100,000). Lakini, ole wake! hawezi kumdanganya Mungu; wala hawezi kumdanganya Ibilisi. La hasha! Laana ya Mungu tayari iko juu yako, na juu ya kila kitu ulicho nacho. Na kesho, Ibilisi atakapotwaa roho yako, je, hatasema, “Mali yako yote inakufaa nini?” Je, itanunua mto wa kuweka kichwa chako katika ziwa la moto uwakao kwa kiberiti? Au itakununulia kikombe cha “maji ya kulowesha ulimi wako” unapoteswa katika mwali huo?” Ee, fuata mwongozo wenye hekima uliotolewa hapa, ili Mungu asikuambie, “Mpumbavu wewe!”

Kwa hiyo, ujanja huu wa kujichezea akili hautasaidia. Hautakulinda dhidi ya ghadhabu ya Mungu wala uovu na nguvu za Ibilisi. Tayari umethibitishwa kuwa unaweka moyo wako juu ya mali zako ikiwa unawekeza tena kila kitu ulicho nacho kinachozidi mahitaji ya maisha, ili kuongeza pesa juu ya pesa, nyumba juu ya nyumba, au shamba juu ya shamba, bila kuwapa maskini angalau sehemu ya kumi ya mapato yako (kiwango cha Wayahudi). Kwa njia yoyote ile ambayo mali zako zinaongezeka, iwe kwa kazi au bila kazi; iwe kwa biashara, urithi, au njia nyingine yoyote; isipokuwa ukarimu wako uongezeke kwa kiwango hicho hicho; isipokuwa utoe sehemu kamili ya kumi ya mali zako na mapato yako ya kudumu na ya mara kwa mara; bila shaka unaweka moyo wako juu ya dhahabu yako, nayo “itakula mwili wako kama moto!”4

Ukaidi wa moyo wa uchoyo

Lakini, ee! Ni nani awezaye kumshawishi tajiri kwamba ameweka moyo wake juu ya mali? Kwa zaidi ya nusu karne nimezungumzia jambo hili kwa uwazi wote nilioweza. Lakini matokeo yamekuwa madogo kama nini! Nina shaka kama katika muda wote huo nimewashawishi hata bahili hamsini kwamba wana uchoyo. Mpenda pesa alipoelezwa kwa uwazi kabisa na kuchorwa kwa rangi nzito zaidi, ni nani aliyejiona kuwa anaelezewa? Ni nani ambaye Mungu na wote waliomjua walisema kumhusu, “Wewe ndiye mtu huyo!” Ikiwa Mungu anazungumza na yeyote kati yenu mliopo hapa, ee, msizibe masikio yenu! Badala yake semeni, pamoja na Zakayo, “Tazama, Bwana, nusu ya mali yangu nawapa maskini; na ikiwa nimemdhulumu mtu yeyote, namrudishia mara nne.” Hakumaanisha kwamba alikuwa amefanya hivyo zamani; bali kwamba aliazimia kufanya hivyo kuanzia wakati huo na kuendelea. Nakusihi mbele za Mungu, ewe mpenda pesa, “nenda ukafanye vivyo hivyo!”

Nina ujumbe kutoka kwa Mungu kwako, ewe tajiri! Utake kusikia au usitake. Mali zimeongezeka kwako; nawe, kwa kuhatarisha roho yako, “usiweke moyo wako juu yake!” Mshukuru Yeye aliyekupa talanta hiyo, uwezo mkubwa hivyo wa kutenda mema. Hata hivyo, usithubutu kuzifurahia, ila kwa hofu na kutetemeka, “Jihadhari usije ukazishikilia, ukanaswa na kuangamia.” Usizifanye kuwa lengo lako, furaha yako kuu, utoshelevu wako, au mungu wako! Hakikisha kwamba hutazamii kupata furaha katika pesa, wala katika kitu chochote kinachoweza kununuliwa kwa pesa; iwe ni kutosheleza tamaa ya mwili, tamaa ya macho, au kiburi cha uzima.

Lakini tushughulikie mambo moja moja; na kila mmoja wenu ahakikishe anaitendea nafsi yake kwa uaminifu. Ikiwa yeyote kati yenu sasa ana mali mara mbili, tatu, au nne zaidi ya alizokuwa nazo alipoona uso wangu kwa mara ya kwanza, ajichunguze kwa uaminifu na kuona kama hajaweka moyo wake, si moja kwa moja juu ya pesa au mali zenyewe, basi juu ya baadhi ya vitu vinavyoweza kununuliwa kwa pesa; jambo ambalo ni sawa na hilo. Mtume Yohana anaviweka vyote chini ya jina hilo la jumla, ulimwengu; na tamaa yake, au kutafuta furaha ndani yake, chini ya usemi huu, “kuupenda ulimwengu.”

Kufafanua “ulimwengu”

Anaugawa katika matawi matatu: “tamaa ya mwili, tamaa ya macho, na kiburi cha uzima.” Jichunguzeni kwa haki kuhusu mambo haya.

  • Kwanza, kuhusu “tamaa ya mwili.” Ninaamini hii humaanisha kutafuta furaha katika vitu vinavyoridhisha hisi. Kwa kutoa mfano mmoja: Je, hamtafuti furaha yenu katika kuongeza raha ya kuonja? Kwa kusema wazi zaidi: Je, mnakula chakula kingi zaidi, au kilichoandaliwa kwa ustadi zaidi, kuliko mlivyofanya miaka kumi au ishirini iliyopita? Je, hamnywi vinywaji vingi zaidi, au vinywaji vya gharama kubwa zaidi, kuliko mlivyofanya wakati huo? Je, bado mnalala kwenye kitanda kigumu kama kile mlichokuwa nacho zamani, ikiwa afya yenu inaruhusu? Kugusia jambo moja zaidi: je, sasa mkiwa matajiri mnafunga mara nyingi kama mlivyofanya mlipokuwa maskini? Kwa kila sababu, je, hamkupaswa kufanya hivyo mara nyingi zaidi badala ya mara chache zaidi? Ninaogopa dhamiri zenu wenyewe zinawahukumu. Hamko safi katika jambo hili.
  • Tawi la pili la kuupenda ulimwengu, “tamaa ya macho,” lina wigo mpana zaidi. Tunaweza kulielewa kuwa kutafuta furaha kwa kuridhisha mawazo (jambo linalofanywa hasa kwa kutumia macho), kwa vitu vya fahari, au vipya, au vizuri (ikiwa vyote hivyo haviwezi kuwekwa katika kundi moja; kwa kuwa vitu vya fahari au vizuri havipendezi tena baada ya kupoteza sifa ya kuwa vipya). Lakini, je, si vitu vilivyo duni zaidi vinavyopendeza maadamu ni vipya? Je, baadhi yenu, kwa sababu tu ya upya, hamtafuti sehemu kubwa ya furaha yenu katika kitu hicho duni kuliko vyote—mavazi? Je, hamtumii pesa nyingi zaidi, au (ambayo ni sawa) muda au juhudi zaidi, kuyashughulikia kuliko mlivyofanya zamani? Nina shaka kwamba hamfanyi hivyo ili kumpendeza Mungu. Basi mnamridhisha Ibilisi. Ikiwa miaka kadhaa iliyopita mliacha mapambo yasiyo ya lazima—mikunjo ya mapambo ya shingo na mikono, shanga, kofia za matundu, kofia mbaya na zisizopendeza,5 vitambaa vya kitani vya gharama kubwa, na lesi za bei ghali—je, hamjayavaa tena, mkikaidi dini na akili?6

Huenda mkasema kwamba sasa mna uwezo wa kumudu gharama hiyo. Huu ni upuuzi mtupu. Ni nani aliyewaongezea mali yenu; au (tukisema kwa usahihi) aliwakopesha? Na tukisema kwa usahihi zaidi, ni nani aliyeziweka mikononi mwenu kwa muda kama wasimamizi wake; huku akiwaeleza wakati huohuo madhumuni aliyowakabidhi mali hizo? Je, mna uwezo wa kupoteza mali za Bwana wenu, ambazo mtawajibika kwa kila kipande chake; au kuzitumia kwa njia nyingine yoyote isipokuwa ile aliyoiagiza waziwazi? Ondoeni wimbo huu mwovu wa kishetani! Usitoke tena vinywani mwenu. Kisingizio hiki cha “kuwa na uwezo” wa kumwibia Mungu ni wimbo hasa wa kuzimu.

Je, hamjui kwamba Mungu aliwakabidhi pesa hizo (kila kitu kinachozidi kile kinachonunua mahitaji ya familia zenu) ili kuwalisha wenye njaa, kuwavisha walio uchi, kuwasaidia wageni, wajane, na yatima; na kwa kweli, kuzitumia kadiri zinavyoweza kuwatosha, kupunguza mahitaji ya wanadamu wote? Mnawezaje, mnathubutuje, kumwibia Bwana wenu kwa kuzitumia kwa kusudi lingine lolote? Alipowakabidhi kiasi kidogo, je, hakukikabidhi ili mtumie kiasi hicho chote kutenda mema? Na alipowakabidhi zaidi, je, hakukabidhi pesa hizo za ziada ili mtende mema mengi zaidi kadiri uwezo wenu ulivyoongezeka? Je, mlikuwa na haki zaidi ya kupoteza pauni moja, shilingi moja, au senti moja kuliko mlivyokuwa nayo hapo awali? Kwa hiyo, hamna haki zaidi sasa ya kutosheleza tamaa ya mwili au tamaa ya macho kuliko mlivyokuwa nayo mlipokuwa ombaomba. La hasha! Msimlipe Bwana wenu mwenye fadhili kwa namna duni hivyo! Badala yake, kadiri anavyowakabidhi zaidi, ndivyo mnapaswa kuwa waangalifu zaidi kutumia kila senti jinsi alivyoagiza.

Kutumia kila senti kama malaika wanavyofanya

Enyi malaika wa Mungu, watumishi wake mnaotimiza mapenzi yake daima: Bwana wetu wa wote amewakabidhi ninyi pia talanta zilizo za thamani zaidi kuliko dhahabu na fedha ili mhudumu katika nyadhifa zenu mbalimbali kwa ajili ya warithi wa wokovu. Je, hamtumii kila senti ya kile mlichopokea kwa kusudi lile lile mlilopewa? Naye hakutuagiza tufanye mapenzi yake duniani kama yanavyofanywa na ninyi mbinguni? Ndugu, tunafanya nini! Na tuamke! Na tusimame! Na tuwaige watumishi hao wawakao kama miali ya moto! Na tutumie nafsi, miili, na mali zetu zote kulingana na mapenzi ya Bwana wetu! Na tumpe Mungu vitu vilivyo vya Mungu; yaani, sisi wenyewe wote na kila kitu tulicho nacho!

Wengi wa wale wanaoweka mioyo yao juu ya mali mali zao zinapoongezeka, hufanya hivyo kwa njia isiyo ya moja kwa moja, kama katika baadhi ya mifano niliyotaja hapo awali. Lakini kuna wengine wanaofanya hivyo moja kwa moja zaidi, nao kwa kweli ni “wapenda pesa.” Wanazipenda kwa ajili yake zenyewe; si tu kwa ajili ya vitu wanavyoweza kununua. Lakini uovu huu haupatikani mara nyingi kwa watoto au vijana; hupatikana tu, au hasa, kwa wazee—wale wanaohitaji pesa kwa kiwango kidogo zaidi na walio na muda mchache zaidi wa kuzifurahia.

Je, jambo hili halingemfanya mtu afikiri kwamba katika visa vingi ni uovu wa adhabu; uovu unaoadhibu dhambi; kwamba mtu anapokuwa ameficha talanta yake ya thamani ardhini kwa miaka mingi, Mungu humkabidhi kwa Shetani ili amwadhibu kwa upendo wake uliopitiliza kwa talanta hiyo? Hapo ndipo anapozidi kuteswa na “njaa hiyo ya dhahabu iliyo ya kuchukiza” ambayo haiwezi kamwe kutoshelezwa. La, ni kweli kabisa kama anavyosema mpagani mwenyewe: “Kadiri pesa zinavyoongezeka, ndivyo upendo wa pesa unavyoongezeka; nazo huongezeka kwa kiwango kilekile.” Ni kama ugonjwa wa kuvimba mwili kwa maji: kadiri unavyokunywa, ndivyo kiu yako inavyoongezeka, mpaka kiu hiyo isiyoweza kuzimwa ikutumbukize katika moto ambao hautazimwa kamwe!

“Lakini je, hakuna njia,” mnaweza kuuliza, “ya kuzuia au kutibu ugonjwa huu wa kutisha?” Kuna njia moja ya kuuzuia ambayo pia ni tiba yake; nami naamini hakuna nyingine chini ya mbingu. Hii ndiyo njia: Baada ya kupata (kwa kufuata tahadhari zilizotolewa hapo juu) kila kitu mnachoweza, na kuokoa kila kitu mnachoweza, huku msikikose chochote, msitumie pauni moja, shilingi moja, wala senti moja kutosheleza tamaa ya mwili, tamaa ya macho, au kiburi cha uzima; wala kwa lengo lolote jingine isipokuwa kumpendeza na kumtukuza Mungu. Mmeepuka mwamba ulio upande wa kulia; jihadharini na ule ulio upande wa kushoto. Pili. Msiweke akiba. Msijiwekee hazina duniani, bali toeni kila kitu mnachoweza; yaani, kila kitu mlicho nacho. Nawapa changamoto watu wote duniani, naam, malaika wote mbinguni, wapate njia nyingine yoyote ya kuondoa sumu iliyomo katika mali.

Ushauri wa mwisho wa Wesley

Niongeze neno moja zaidi. Baada ya kuwahudumia kwa miaka kati ya sitini na sabini; nikiwa na macho hafifu, mikono inayotetemeka, na miguu inayoyumba, nawapa ushauri mmoja zaidi kabla sijazama mavumbini. Zingatieni maneno haya ya Mtakatifu Paulo: “Wale wanaotamani,” au kujitahidi “kuwa matajiri,” mara hiyohiyo “huanguka katika majaribu.” Naam, wanaingia katika shimo refu la majaribu ambalo hakuna kitu chochote isipokuwa nguvu za Mwenyezi Mungu ziwezazo kuwaokoa. “Hutumbukia katika mtego”—neno hili hasa humaanisha mtego wa chuma, ambao humponda papo hapo mnyama anayeingia humo vipande vipande—“na katika tamaa mbalimbali za kipumbavu na zenye madhara, ambazo huwatumbukiza watu katika uharibifu na upotevu.” Ninyi hasa, kuliko watu wote, mnaofanikiwa sasa duniani, msisahau kamwe maneno haya ya kutisha! Njia yenu inateleza kiasi gani! Kila hatua ni hatari kiasi gani! Bwana Mungu awawezeshe kuona hatari yenu na kuwafanya muielewe kwa undani! Ee, na muamke “baada ya mfano wake, na kuridhika nao!”

Niruhusuni niwasogelee zaidi kidogo. Huenda nisawasumbue tena kuhusu jambo hili. Nina huzuni kwa ajili yenu “mlio matajiri katika ulimwengu huu.” Je, mnatoa kila kitu mnachoweza? Ninyi mnaopokea £500 kwa mwaka na kutumia £200 tu, je, mnampa Mungu tena £300? La sivyo, kwa hakika mnamwibia Mungu £300 hizo. Ninyi mnaopokea £200 na kutumia £100 tu, je, mnampa Mungu £100 hizo? La sivyo, mnampokonya kiasi hicho hicho.

Visingizio

“La, je, siwezi kufanya nitakavyo na mali yangu mwenyewe?” Hapo ndipo msingi wa kosa lenu ulipo. Mali hiyo si yenu. Haiwezi kuwa yenu, isipokuwa ninyi ni Bwana wa mbingu na dunia.

“Hata hivyo, sina budi kuwatunza watoto wangu.” Bila shaka. Lakini kwa njia gani? Kwa kuwafanya matajiri? Basi huenda mkawafanya kuwa wapagani, kama baadhi yenu mlivyofanya tayari.

“Basi nifanye nini?” Bwana, zungumza na mioyo yao, la sivyo mhubiri anazungumza bure! Waachieni kiasi cha kutosha cha kuishi, si kwa uvivu na anasa, bali kwa kufanya kazi kwa uaminifu. Na ikiwa hamna watoto, ni kwa kanuni gani ya Kimaandiko au ya kiakili mnaweza kuwaachia zaidi ya senti moja, kiasi kinachozidi gharama ya kuwazika? Tafadhali fikirini, mnayafaidi nini kwa kile mnachoacha nyuma? Kuna tofauti gani kama mtaacha nyuma yenu £10,000 au jozi 10,000 za viatu na buti?

Ee, msiache chochote nyuma yenu! Tuma kila kitu ulicho nacho mbele yako katika ulimwengu bora zaidi! Kikopeshe, kikopeshe chote kwa Bwana, naye atakulipa tena! Je, kuna hatari yoyote kwamba kweli yake itashindwa? Imewekwa imara kama nguzo za mbingu. Harakeni, harakeni, ndugu zangu, harakeni—msije mkaitwa kuondoka kabla hamjaweka mali zenu chini ya dhamana hii! Jambo hili likishafanyika, mnaweza kusema kwa ujasiri, “Sasa sina jambo lingine la kufanya ila kufa! Baba, mikononi mwako naiweka roho yangu! Njoo, Bwana Yesu! Njoo upesi!” ~

1 £ ni alama ya pauni ya Uingereza. Ni vigumu kwa kiasi fulani kulinganisha thamani ya pesa katika karne na tamaduni mbalimbali. Lakini, ili kutoa wazo la jumla, huenda kibarua wa kawaida nchini Uingereza mwaka 1780 alipata £2-3 kwa mwezi. Hiyo ingelingana na kupata takriban $300-400 kwa mwezi katika uchumi wa Marekani wa leo.

2 Kama ilivyotajwa katika tanbihi iliyotangulia, huenda mshahara wa wastani wa kibarua wa kawaida wakati huo ulikuwa karibu £30 kwa mwaka.

3 Takriban £1.

4 Kutaja kwa Wesley zaka hapa kunaweza kuonekana kana kwamba anahimiza tu kutoa zaka ya kawaida. Lakini tambua kwamba muktadha unahusu “kuwekeza tena.” Wengi huhisi kwamba wanapaswa kuwekeza tena faida ili waweze kupata zaidi na hivyo kuwa na zaidi ya kutoa baadaye. Wesley ana shaka na “hekima” hiyo na anahimiza kutoa angalau 10% kwa maskini mara moja badala ya kuiwekeza tena. Wazo la kuwekeza tena faida ili kuwa na zaidi ya kutoa baadaye lina vishawishi vingi. Wengi wanaonekana kutofika kamwe zaidi ya kuwekeza tena; badala ya kutoa zaidi baadaye, wanawekeza tena ... na tena ... na tena. Na pesa hazifiki kamwe kwa maskini.

5 Bila shaka yoyote, Wesley anazungumzia kofia fulani ya mtindo aliyoiona kuwa mbaya, si kofia za aina zote kwa ujumla.

6 Katika ujumbe huu, Wesley hafiki kamwe kwenye kufafanua kipengele cha tatu, “kiburi cha uzima.”
